messages:
maria: Heads up — planning to flip the internal proxy to emit the new route header (`X-RW-Route-V2`) next week. This will change how quotas are attributed for multi-tenant requests.

sam: wait — how will this interact with existing SDKs that set `X-RW-Route` today?

maria: Good q. We want servers to prefer V2 when present, but fall back to V1. The tricky part is quota aggregation: V2 can encode multiple route hints.

jordan: Can you paste an example of the new header format?

maria: Sure — example: ```X-RW-Route-V2: route=ingest,shard=eu-west-1;prio=100``` It’s semicolon-delimited keypairs, and we support comma-separated routes for fanout.

lee: :eyes: That sounds like a breaking parsing change for some lightweight clients. Are we planning an SDK shim?

maria: We should. Proposed plan: servers accept both; SDKS should start emitting V2 opt-in via a feature flag in the next minor release. Full switch (stop emitting V1) after 60 days.

sam: For telemetry, do we want Console dashboards to show both route versions during the transition? Product will want a single canonical view.

olivia: I can add a compatibility layer in the Console: a translation step that normalizes V1->V2 for charts, then we can surface 'unknown' when parsing fails.

jordan: Quotas: if a request has both V1 and V2, do we dedupe? e.g., old `X-RW-Route: ingest` and new `X-RW-Route-V2: route=ingest,shard=eu-west-1`

maria: Server-side rule: prefer V2. If V2 present, use it for quota attribution. If only V1 present, use the old behavior. We'll add an audit log entry when V1 is used and V2 could have been used.

sam: SDK implications — Python and TS SDKs need a non-breaking opt-in flag, default off, to emit V2. Go SDK historically has simplest headers; we should align behavior.

lee: I can put together a tiny shim: if `routeHints` is an array, serialize to V2; otherwise keep V1. That avoids a forced break for customers.

jordan: Tests: need server + SDK e2e that validates quota buckets still sum correctly during canary. Also make sure sampling telemetry includes both header types.

maria: Agreed. Action items: (1) eng-platform: deploy proxy that accepts both and logs mismatches (maria) (2) sdks: add opt-in flag + serializer (sam, lee, jordan split) (3) console: normalization shim for charts (olivia) (4) product/ops: run a 2-week canary and spot-check quota deltas (sam).

sam: Timeline?

maria: Canary deploy Wednesday (1755650000), monitor for 2 weeks, ramp if no anomalies, deprecate V1 emit in ~60 days post-ramp.

deploy-bot: live-config update: proxy will add `X-RW-Route-V2` parsing at 2025-03-12T14:00:00Z. :rocket:

jordan: Noted — planning to add unit tests for serialization, and a fuzz test for malformed V2 tokens.

lee: One UX ask: when SDKs default to opt-in, can we add an obvious opt-out env var for internal customers? Some infra teams prefer explicit behavior.

maria: Yes — default opt-in = false. Env var `RW_ROUTE_V2=1` flips it. We'll add deprecation docs and a migration checklist.

sam: Also add telemetry tag `route_header_version` to traces so we can roll back quickly if quota mismatch spikes.

olivia: Console will show a small banner during canary: "Routing header migration in progress — data may include mixed versions."

maria: Okay looks like we have alignment. We'll sync on a short RFC tonight and link it in this thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
